contract: One MCP server that a tenant added at run time (Streamable HTTP, bearer token from an integration/secrets reference or from a tenant OAuth connection through the host's OAuth Need), turned into a ready integration/mcp-client runtime config only after three steps in fixed order: integration/egress-policy resolve/3 admits the https URL and every resolved address is public, else {:egress, reason} with egress-policy's own reason and nothing later runs; one check before connecting, the value dropped: for the reference form %{ref, scope} one integration/secrets resolution, expired giving credentials_expired and any other failure or a raise, throw or exit of the secrets function giving credentials_unavailable (unchanged byte for byte); for the OAuth form %{oauth: connection_id} one call of the host's OAuth Need oauth.(%{tenant, connection_id}), {:ok, binary} passing and every other answer (reauthorization_required, revoked, any other error, a malformed answer, a raise, throw or exit) giving credentials_unavailable; then Elzoo.McpClient.configure/1 with Elzoo.McpClient.RuntimeBinding and the egress host, port and whole checked address set (network :public), whose zero-arity credential Need resolves the reference, or asks the OAuth Need, again at each request, never storing the token and giving {:ok, token} or {:error, :credentials_unavailable}; the ready client calls it once per HTTP request plus twice around each listing and each tool call for redaction (measured: a tool call 3). configure/1 takes exact keys with exactly one of secrets and oauth, the one of the credential form (connection_id 1..128 bytes of printable UTF-8), refuses a URL query and calls no Need; inspect shows tenant and server text only. list_tools/2 keys the unchanged ready listing or unavailable{credentials_expired | credentials_unavailable | a finite reason of the ready client} by {tenant, server}, after the check. Tool calls stay the ready connect/2, admission/3, context/3 (bound to the admission's intent key, so a session of another runtime config, with another tenant, server text or URL, cannot execute an intent admitted under this one) and call_tool/3 path. Errors never echo the URL, host, token or reference; no telemetry or log of its own.
limits: Addresses are as fresh as the admission; after a disconnect the host admits again.

Redirect refusal and the response cap are ex_mcp and integration/mcp-client duties, held by ELZ-282's drift tests; the ELZ-282 loopback runtime tests are the transport evidence. This Piece cannot reach a loopback server through egress-policy, by design: a successful public connect is not exercised and there is no live public endpoint in the evidence.

One tenant credential per server: no per-person lists, no OAuth flow in the Piece, no token cache, no stdio. The OAuth Need, its binding, its Repo and its timeouts are the host's; the Piece decides only on what the Need answers. When the Need is integration/oauth-client's, one request can wait for the time a call holds its transaction (the pool queue wait, the row-lock wait, exchange_timeout_ms and the time of its Needs), the host Repo's :timeout must exceed that time (oauth-client's Consumer Needs, #886), and each Need call is one database transaction; the ready client calls the Need before, during and after each request (during inside call_timeout_ms or handshake_timeout_ms; before and after for redaction, inside call_tool/3's wait of call_timeout_ms plus 5,000 ms around a tool call and unbounded around a whole listing, where a slow Need only delays it), so the host keeps its waits within those bounds (a longer wait during a page request fails the listing with the ready client's finite reason, and around a tool call makes it unknown{timeout}, after a successful response an unknown outcome after the tool ran; by the code path, not measured); admit/1 inside a host transaction gets :in_transaction and refuses credentials_unavailable.

The check before the call and the credential Need are two samples of the Secrets resolver or of the OAuth Need; a rotation, refresh or revocation between them is possible. The check does not apply the ready client's 24-byte and fixed-string rule: such an OAuth token is admitted and then refused before each request.

mcp-client's session ledger takes at most 64 distinct tokens per session: a refreshed OAuth token is used from the next request on up to that bound, a 65th distinct token is refused (credentials_unavailable) and the host must reconnect. Carried mcp-client behavior, not tested here; issue #912 is the follow-up repair.

The pairing and the list_tools/2 match tie tenant, server text and URL only: configs that differ only in credential (form, reference or connection id), addresses or bounds share the intent identity (so a config admitted again can recover an intent), and one credential per {tenant, server} is the host's duty.
The ready client's Adapter context is not opaque: host code that edits a context's session or key bypasses the pairing.
No claim about what a tool does. Finite tests; no proof is claimed.

grounding.claim: Named acceptance groups: egress_first (http, IP literal, non-allowlisted host, wrong port, nxdomain, resolver raise, 10.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1 and a mixed answer give egress-policy's reason with no secrets or Secrets resolver call, no new ExMCP.Client process and no socket or transport module among the Piece's BEAM imports), admission (exact host, port, sorted addresses, network and server; the Need resolves again on each call; a query, a forged policy struct and a URL over the ready 512-byte endpoint bound are configuration, invalid UTF-8 is egress malformed), credentials, keying (distinct {tenant, server} keys and rt1 identities for one ref; a session of another tenant, server text or URL, or a build-time session, is not listed), pairing (a session of another runtime config, with another tenant, server text or URL, cannot execute an intent admitted under this one, with a real delivery/effect-intent owner and the ready client's loopback server), secrecy, golden_bearer (recorded on the base before the OAuth form: the bearer client config fields and its Need's results and Secrets call counts), oauth_admission (one OAuth Need call at the check, given tenant and connection id; the Need asks again at each call), oauth_loopback (the OAuth credential Need on the ready client's loopback mode lists and calls a tool and a recording Plug before ExMCP.HttpPlug sees the token on every request; measured Need calls connect 1, three-page listing 5, tool call 3), oauth_refresh (a token switched by the test between two tool calls of one session is seen on the next request), oauth_refusal (reauthorization_required, revoked, unavailable, other errors, malformed answers and a raise, throw or exit refuse at admit/1 and list_tools/2 with no request on the session; an egress refusal calls no Need), oauth_configure (Need and form combinations, connection_id bounds, inspect), and the checked example; the credential-before-egress, first-address-only, server-only-key, URL-dropped-from-the-list_tools-match any-policy-struct and OAuth-check-skipped negative controls fail under temporary edits. Finite evidence, not proof.

ex_mcp 1.8.1 at its exact pin, reached only through the ready integration/mcp-client runtime mode, used unchanged with integration/egress-policy and integration/secrets; pinned-address transport, redirect refusal and the response cap are the ready client's, held by its drift tests.

The host supplies a truthful egress resolver that bounds its own time, a truthful secrets function and Secrets resolver with each scope bound to one tenant and one server or a truthful OAuth Need bound to the tenant's own connection, starts ex_mcp and a DynamicSupervisor, and supplies the recipient and owner of each tool call; the ready client's named assumption that a 401 or 403 means nothing ran.

telemetry.contract: No Elzoo event and no log of its own, as the ready client: ex_mcp emits upstream [:ex_mcp, ...] events and debug logs that consumer-installed handlers may see (the consumer's responsibility). Own events: a future task when a consumer needs them.

config.contract: Construction-time only through configure/1: tenant, server text, URL, egress policy and resolver Need, credential (reference with its secrets function, or OAuth connection id with its OAuth Need) and the ready client bounds with the ready ranges and defaults. No hot update; a changed URL, policy or credential is a new config, admitted again.

control.contract: The Piece owns no process; the host owns the session (Elzoo.McpClient.close/1). Dispatch and recovery of a tool call are the delivery/effect-intent owner's Control.
